fields.meta_title: Real Estate Landing Page Builder for Agents | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a real estate landing page for a listing or a home valuation, and send every lead to the right agent and into your CRM.
fields.h1: Build a Real Estate Landing Page for Every Listing and Lead
fields.hero_description: Create a real estate landing page from one prompt, and route each buyer or seller lead to the agent who should call back.
fields.explore_cta: Build My Real Estate Landing Page
fields.features_heading: What Every Realtor Landing Page Needs
fields.features_subheading: The page a buyer or seller sees, and the routing that puts their name in front of an agent the same day.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that separate buyers from sellers

Emergent writes the form around the lead you want: an address and a sale timeline from a seller, a price range from a buyer. Each answer lands in its own column of the table.
fields.feature_2:
Each lead assigned to one agent

Assign leads by zip code or by listing, and name a backup agent for days off. The agent gets a Slack message or an email with the answers, and each assignment is logged.
fields.feature_3:
New leads in Follow Up Boss or your CRM

Follow Up Boss or any other CRM with an API receives each lead along with its source and its listing. Agents keep working in the tool they already open every morning.
fields.feature_4:
Price and photo changes by message

Send Emergent a message to cut the price by $10,000 or mark the home under contract. The page updates at the same address, and leads saved before the change stay put.
fields.feature_5:
A page for each listing or farm area

Ask for a page for each listing or each neighborhood you farm, with its own headline and photos. All of them write to one lead table that names the page behind each lead.
fields.feature_6:
Code export and a brokerage domain

Pages, routing rules, and the lead table export to your GitHub on paid plans. Your brokerage's custom domain is included and uses credits, or the code can run on your own host.

fields.usecase_heading: Real Estate Landing Pages by Lead Type
fields.tab_content_1:
Owners who plan to sell this season, sorted from the rest

Owners who type an address into Cedar Row Realty's home value page also say when they plan to sell. Anyone selling within 90 days reaches listing agent Dana Ruiz as a Slack direct message. She prices the home herself before she calls. Owners further out join a monthly market email.
fields.tab_content_2:
Who walked through 1412 Larch Lane without an agent

On Sunday afternoon, visitors at 1412 Larch Lane scan the QR code on the door sign and sign in on their own phones. The form asks for contact details and whether they already have an agent. At 5 PM the host agent, Marcus Bell, gets an email listing the 12 of 31 visitors who answered no.
fields.tab_content_3:
Three showing slots on a single listing page

The price and three showing slots share the first screen of the page for 27 Birch Avenue, listed at $689,000. A buyer who picks Saturday at 11:00 AM reaches Follow Up Boss as a property inquiry with the address attached. From there, the listing agent's usual follow-up plan in Follow Up Boss picks it up.
fields.tab_content_4:
Same-day calls for sellers closing within 30 days

Ridgeway Home Buyers' cash offer page asks sellers what the house needs and when they want to close. Requests from sellers who need to close within 30 days go on that day's call list for the acquisitions manager, Leo Grant. Everyone else gets a written offer by email after a drive-by.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Real Estate Landing Page
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan a real estate landing page around one offer, keep its copy within Fair Housing rules, and assign every lead.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick one visitor and one ask
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Repeat the promise the ad made
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Describe the home, not the buyer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Ask only what the callback needs
fields.howto_step_1_des: A seller page and a buyer page need different questions, which is why they belong on separate pages. Decide who the page is for and the one action it asks for: an address in exchange for a price opinion, or a time for a showing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Housing ads on Facebook and Instagram run in Meta's Special Ad Category, with fewer targeting options than other ads. The page does the sorting the audience settings cannot: repeat the ad's promise in the headline and put the qualifying question near the top.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The Fair Housing Act bars housing ads that state a preference based on race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, or national origin. Write about the rooms and the commute. Leave out who the home would suit, such as 'perfect for a young couple'.
fields.howto_step_4_des: A phone number and one qualifying answer cover most pages: a sale timeline from sellers, a price range from buyers. Leave the other questions for the call, where the agent can explain why each one matters and the visitor can answer in full.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the assignment rule down before the first ad runs: which agent owns which listing, and who covers weekends. Agree as well on how soon a seller lead should hear back. A page with no owner collects names that nobody calls.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Search across every home on the MLS runs through IDX, which lets MLS participants show other brokers' listings on sites they control. Keep that search on the brokerage website and link to it. The landing page stays on its one offer.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Compare leads by source every week
fields.howto_step_7_des: Tag each ad and yard-sign link with a source. Every Monday, put leads beside booked appointments for each source. A page that collects plenty of names and few appointments needs a sharper qualifying question before it needs more traffic.

The galleries show a hero photo and a form; the posts list tips. None shows what happens after a seller types an address or a visitor signs in at the door: which agent hears about it, what the CRM receives, and which lead gets a call today. This page defines the term up top for the AI Overview, then shows four working real estate pages by job (seller valuation, open house sign-in, single listing, cash offer), each with its routing and data behind it, plus a how-to grounded in Fair Housing advertising rules, Meta's housing ad category, NAR's IDX and open house guidance.
